title: Control and Choice
quote: The chief task in life is simply this: to identify and separate matters so that I can say clearly to myself which are externals not under my control, and which have to do with the choices I actually control.
commentary: The most important practice in Stoic philosophy is differentiating between what we can change and what we can’t. What we have influence over and what we don’t. A flight is delayed because of weather—no amount of yelling at an airline representative will end a storm.

title: Education Is Freedom
quote: What is the fruit of these teachings? Only the most beautiful and proper harvest of the truly educated—tranquility, fearlessness, and freedom. We should not trust the masses who say only the free can be educated, but rather the lovers of wisdom who say that only the educated are free.
commentary: Why did you pick up this book? Why pick up any book? Not to seem smarter, not to pass time on the plane, not to hear what you want to hear—there are plenty of easier choices for those things.

title: Be Ruthless to the Things That Don’t Matter
quote: How many have laid waste to your life when you weren’t aware of what you were losing, how much was wasted in pointless grief, foolish joy, greedy desire, and social amusements—how little of your own was left to you. You will realize you are dying before your time!
source: Seneca, On the Brevity of Life, 3.3b
commentary: One of the hardest things to do in life is to say “No.” To invitations, to requests, to obligations, to the stuff that everyone else is doing. Even harder is saying no to certain time-consuming emotions: anger, excitement, distraction, obsession, lust.

title: The Source of Your Anxiety
quote: When I see an anxious person, I ask myself, what do they want? For if a person wasn’t wanting something outside of their own control, why would they be stricken by anxiety?
commentary: Anxiety is almost always a result of wanting something we can't have, or wanting to control something we can't control.
